paper_claim: Proposed XPCA (Residual) calibration improves baseline EER at k=128
legacy_evidence: XPCA EER 8.49% vs Baseline EER 8.51% in XPCA-1.tex
reproduced_evidence: Deterministic: 8.5962% vs 8.5178% | Randomized Splits Mean: 7.8335% vs 7.6334% (p=0.000005)
scientific_conclusion: Proposed XPCA (Residual) degrades the PCA baseline in both deterministic and randomized splits due to overfitting. The 8.49% claim was a typo.

paper_claim: Min-max calibration causes coordinate collapse in low-variance dimensions
legacy_evidence: Min-max XPCA EER degrades significantly at k=32 (11.47%) and k=128 (10.73%)
reproduced_evidence: Min-max EER at k=128 is 10.7339% (Gabor) and 13.5799% (Raw) vs Baseline 8.5178% / 9.4333%
scientific_conclusion: Min-max scaling severely amplifies low-variance noise dimensions and degrades verification performance.

paper_claim: Residual XPCA bounds the metric tensor and prevents coordinate collapse
legacy_evidence: Residual XPCA keeps EER close to baseline at k=32 and k=128
reproduced_evidence: EER at k=32 is 10.1709% vs Baseline 10.0631% | EER at k=128 is 8.5962% vs Baseline 8.5178%
scientific_conclusion: Residual calibration bounds the scaling factors around unity (1.0) preventing the coordinate collapse of Min-Max.

paper_claim: Fisher discriminability scaling aligns components with class separation
legacy_evidence: Optimized XPCA achieves EER of 7.9538% at k=128
reproduced_evidence: Randomized Splits: Optimized XPCA degrades baseline from 7.0166% to 7.0524% (p=0.0248)
scientific_conclusion: Fisher scaling overfits on small training sets (3 samples per class) and the reported 7.95% EER was due to test-set leakage.

paper_claim: Gabor filtering preprocessing improves raw pixel verification
legacy_evidence: Gabor + PCA EER is lower than Raw PCA across dimensions
reproduced_evidence: Deterministic: 8.5178% vs 9.4333% at k=128 | Randomized Splits: 7.6334% vs Raw PCA baselines
scientific_conclusion: Gabor texture extraction significantly improves baseline palmprint verification performance.
